name: Dryden Tract
description: The moraine loop everyone around here measures other trails against. Hardwood forest climbs to a meadow summit with a farm view — the spot to stop, breathe and stretch. The standard loop is 4.3 km; the Big Loop adds the full ridge for 5.8 km and about 169 m of climbing.
parking: Free gravel lot at the trailhead on Alps Rd

pointsOfInterest.name: Farm Overlook
pointsOfInterest.note: Meadow-summit viewpoint over the farm fields, on the southern singletrack network

name: Sudden Tract
description: Dryden's quieter neighbour — rolling moraine trails through mixed forest, right next door on Spragues Rd. The West Loop is 3.1 km, and the Grand Valley Trail links Sudden to Dryden if you want a 7.1 km ridge route between the two tracts.
parking: Free lot at the trailhead on Spragues Rd

name: Drynan Regional Forest
description: Moraine forest with kettle lakes and farm-field lookouts, a few minutes past Dryden and Sudden. A roughly 3.4 km loop with enough up and down to feel like a proper hike, and far fewer people than the city trails.

name: F.W.R. Dickson Wilderness Area
description: A different flavour from the moraine tracts: a 4.8 km figure-of-eight through wetlands, tall-grass prairie and forest, with boardwalks over the kettle lakes. It's famous for its chickadees, which will feed from your hand at the boardwalk. Open 8 a.m. to 8 p.m. daily.
parking: Lot at the entrance off Brant-Waterloo Rd · GRCA property

name: Pinehurst Lake Conservation Area
description: A kettle lake ringed by pine forest on the Brant–Waterloo border, with a sandy beach in summer and trails looping through the pines behind it. The southernmost stop in this set — pair it with a Paris coffee run.
parking: GRCA conservation area — day-use fee at the gate

name: Little Tract
description: A Wellington County forest tract north of the city: a network of winding trails through wetlands and the Oil Well Bog, with small hills running off in every direction — check the mapped paths below before you go, because the network is easy to get turned around in. Free entry.

name: Devil's Creek Trail
description: The short one: 1.6 km of paved trail through the Devil's Creek wetlands and ravine in Blair, with the creek and its little waterfall below the path. Good for a quick evening walk when a full hike isn't on.
parking: Street parking near Blair Rd / Bismark Dr

name: rare Charitable Research Reserve
description: A 900+ acre research reserve where the Grand River bends past alvar, cliffs and old-growth maples. The Grand River Trail runs 5.0 km, with the Maple Lane, Grand Allée, ECO and Alvar trails branching off it. Free to visit.
parking: Free parking at the Resource House, 1679 Blair Rd

name: Grand Trunk Trail
description: Ten kilometres along the Grand River from downtown Galt up to Blair, on the old Grand Trunk rail bed. Flat, riverside and easy to join at either end — the downtown Galt access below puts you on it by the riverfront.
parking: Downtown Galt lots near the riverfront

name: Cambridge to Paris Rail Trail
description: The big one: 18 km of rail trail up the Grand River from Galt to Paris, almost all of it shaded riverbank. Hike a section out-and-back from the Water St trailhead, or go point to point and earn lunch in Paris.
parking: Trailhead lot at 210 Water St S

name: Dumfries Conservation Area
description: The in-city escape: a GRCA woodland on Dunbar Rd with a pond and easy looping trails through the trees. The one to pick when you want woods without the drive south.
parking: Lot off Dunbar Rd · GRCA property

name: Shade's Mills Conservation Area
description: The city's big GRCA park: about 10 km of trails through forest around the Shade's Mills reservoir, plus a beach on the lake in summer. Enough network to build anything from a 2 km stroll to a full morning loop.
parking: GRCA conservation area — day-use fee at the gate
